newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS - Aegon buys Providian insurance arm.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Aegon buys Providian insurance arm.

text.p: Dutch Aegon NV, one of the world's largest insurance firms, said on Monday it would buy the insurance activities of the Providian Corp of the United States in a deal worth $3.5 billion.
The deal is one the largest to date in a rapidly consolidating life-insurance industry, beset by high costs and fierce competition from banks and mutual fund companies.

"Consolidation in the insurance sector will certainly continue in Europe and the United States. Market shares are diminishing and European union will accelerate this process," said IRIS analyst Bart van der Feen.
Aegon said the deal, expected to be concluded in the first half of 1997, would involve a tax-free share swap.
Providian shareholders would receive Aegon shares worth $2.62 billion and Aegon USA would take over loans worth $780 million and preferred stock worth $100 million.
Analysts welcomed the deal, echoing Aegon's announcement that it expected the transaction to "have an immediate positive impact on its earnings per share".
"This is a very positive acquisition. Looking at the EPS, we are expecting an increase of between four and eight percent," said Van der Feen, adding he was maintaining a buy rating on Aegon shares.
"One of the main points is that the deal is to be mainly financed internally without a major share issue," he added.
Aegon stock jumped early on the news, rising 7.30 guilders or 7.4 percent to 106.50 guilders amid an otherwise quiet but firm Amsterdam bourse.

Providian Corp is based in Louisville, Kentucky and is active throughout the United States. It is divided into four divisions -- Providian Bancorp, Direct Insurance Group, Agency Group and Capital Management Group.
Aegon, based in the Hague, has total assets of around 150 billion guilders ($86 billion) and operates in the Netherlands, the United States, Britain, Spain and Hungary, it said.
In the first nine months of 1996 it had total net profit of 1.1 billion guilders ($630.7 million) and total revenues of 18.2 billion guilders ($10.4 billion).
